tip.problem: Your page downloads JavaScript code that is never actually executed on the page.
tip.fix: Split large script bundles into smaller files and import libraries only where needed.
tip.example: Instead of importing an entire 500 KB utility library, import only the specific functions you use.

tip.problem: Your stylesheets include CSS rules that do not style any element on the current page.
tip.fix: Remove dead CSS rules or split your stylesheet into page-specific CSS files.
tip.example: Avoid loading an entire CSS framework across every page if only a few utility classes are needed.

tip.problem: Your images are larger than they need to be, so visitors download extra data.
tip.fix: Compress images and use modern formats like WebP or AVIF.
tip.example: Convert hero.jpg (3 MB) to hero.webp using squoosh.app, often 70% smaller.

tip.problem: Your page downloads JavaScript code that is never actually executed on the page.

tip.problem: Legacy image formats like JPEG and PNG take longer to download than modern compressed formats.
tip.fix: Serve images in modern WebP or AVIF formats for smaller file sizes without losing visual quality.
tip.example: Use the <picture> element to serve WebP or AVIF with a JPEG fallback.

tip.problem: CSS and JavaScript files in the head of your page stop the browser from displaying content until they finish downloading.
tip.fix: Add the defer or async attribute to script tags, and inline critical above-the-fold CSS.
tip.example: Change <script src="app.js"></script> to <script src="app.js" defer></script>.

tip.problem: Text files (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) are sent across the network uncompressed.
tip.fix: Enable Gzip or Brotli compression on your web server or CDN.
tip.example: In Node/Express, add the compression middleware (app.use(compression())) to shrink responses by up to 70%.
